# Resumed independent D14 review — merged main, qualification pending

**Disposition: no new blocking product or security defect found in the reviewed source; whole-release acceptance is withheld.** The missing qualification and release-policy implementation below remain unresolved. This document is not an accepted D14 report, a publication approval, or a substitute for actual measurement.

Reviewed merge commit: `ee7e5751e5d0df5b285e9d176554314fe60e5dca`.
Reviewed tree: `679e9718a0036ed853e31b0f6e94f70f6fee966e`.
The clean local checkout is `2e98b588edd629fffddcb2bc838944bc3412d85b`; Git independently confirms its exact tree equality with the merge commit. No checkout or source mutation was performed. This resumes the same independent reviewer task/session whose actual initialization is retained here. The prior interim substantive review remains the detailed source-coverage record; no earlier approval is substituted for this review.

## Exact delta and resolved finding

I inspected the actual changed-file inventory and deltas from the reviewed e75 implementation and 7126 pipeline proposal to merged main. There are 52 changed paths. Twenty-one manifest, lock and template-seed files are exactly the coordinated `3.0.0-rc.1` → `3.0.0` transition, including removal of the explicit prerelease alternative in internal peer ranges. The independent read-only comparison admits no other edits in those files. All runtime/compiler/build/native implementation scopes, core mutation scripts and test oracles, parity/indexed fixture code, ordinary CI/security/nightly workflows and performance/security readers compared are unchanged from e75. Relative to exact 7126, the only scripts/workflow difference is the release-contract gate status record. The overlap and bounded post-write visibility fixes remain the exact previously reviewed implementation. `git diff --check` passes.

The nine non-audit RC rows close against the completed source-bound evidence. The audit row remains pending. Final cleanup, per-release P17 and soak rows remain pending. Final-version changelogs and public documentation say prepared/unpublished; they do not assert final registry publication. Quota handoff files preserve checkpoint status, zero credited soak and the release-validator gap. They are not audit evidence.

**D14-001 is resolved in this reviewed tree.** `docs/release/RC-BURN-IN.md:144` now separates the P17 verifier's hard 1,800-second limit, the outer-release G6 target and human maintainer effort. It explicitly retains beta.4's outer-target miss. Actual correction was read in the 72179 delta and confirmed in merged main.

Machine-readable scope inventory: `FINAL-MAIN-DELTA-RECHECK.json`. Versioned archives are not claimed identical merely because implementation source is unchanged. Changed package metadata and documentation also mean the historical full-suite input set is not byte-identical in every respect.

## Completed evidence independently rechecked

I read the original completed RC P17 report from run `39049587766`, attempt 1, and revalidated it with the unchanged performance reader in the reviewed current source. It is explicitly an e75 RC rehearsal, not main/final publication evidence. All 61 original checks pass in 1224.085 seconds. The retained published beta.4 DS12 bytes hash to the reported baseline digest, and its actual native rates match the baseline used for RC comparison. Both original candidate/P17 ZIP sizes and SHA-256 digests match retained GitHub artifact API receipts. No artifacts were downloaded again and no campaign was rerun.

Both twenty-run mobile routes retain empty Lighthouse and independent-observer long-task arrays, correct activation/input response and the original dead/slow controls. Demanding decoder p95/max are 20.9/23.8 ms; all raw correctness, samples and refusal criteria pass the current reader. All three engines contain the required eleven actual skew checks, including immutable success and revoked-resource refusal. The evidence owner’s original journal/cleanup validation and original logs remain retained; I did not replace them with a new producer identity.

I also reapplied current hostile and expression proof validators to the original packed security report: 1686 hostile cases, 30 capability controls, actual retained removed-guard 0/1/0 reports with matching byte hashes, and the 100000-case expression before/mutant/corrected proof. The security harness hashes equal current main. These are original packed RC results, not new final-archive results. See `COMPLETED-E75-P17-RECHECK.json` and `COMPLETED-E75-SECURITY-RECHECK.json`.

The earlier independent raw rechecks of the 252-mutation campaign and six SR14 triples continue to support their unchanged subjects and kill oracles. Original producers remain 0967 and 9851 respectively; no exact-main mutation campaign is claimed. Pure internal version changes do not change the external dependency graph, but final-package sealing and version-sensitive integration still require current qualification. Build/rebuild and route measurements retain their original source/package identities and disclosed applicability; the final target is a distinct package set.

Exact-main ordinary CI `39056716276` is completed/success for ee7, supported by the lead's single live API/CLI observation retained at `work/codex-release-lead/MONDAY-MAIN-CI.json`. This audit did not repeat that network query or download its artifacts. The lead separately reports successful security run `39054836280` on tree-identical 2e98; the retained original six-probe evidence remains the independently inspected security result. Ordinary CI success does not establish the twenty-command timing distribution or final packed qualification.

## Unresolved requirements, distinguished from product defects

1. **Combined-source R17 qualification is missing at this checkpoint.** Six finite helper tests changed the timed command since e75. Its accepted twenty-run p95 570.93 s/max 573.99 s cannot be assigned to ee7. Actual run `39285416133` has been dispatched once by the lead with measured source ee7 and a distinct workflow donor; its result was not yet supplied. Require all twenty normal commands to succeed, the retained all-101 L67 vectors/guards, and actual rank-19 command p95 <600 s. This is a qualification hold, not a demonstrated runtime regression.

2. **Current final packed qualification is pending.** Run `39285412822` targets `v3.0.0` on ee7 and has been dispatched once by the lead. The e75 report cannot substitute for its final-version package bytes, template seeds, source/provenance and actual checks. Review the original completed result when supplied. This is an evidence hold, not a claim that the queued run failed.

3. **P1 release-policy implementation gap: the founder's post-release burn-in deferral is not executable in the current release path.** The lead conveyed the primary founder instruction explicitly deferring the full L62 3600-second active soak to post-release verification; credited time remains zero. The lead also conveyed Monday's explicit audit resumption. The old decision brief has no quota amendment, and Tickets are secondary checkpoint records, so this review does not manufacture primary decision provenance or infer acceptance from them.

   At `scripts/check-release-qualification.mjs:12–16`, final still unconditionally requires `readBurnInReference`/`verifyFinalBurnIn`; no final reference exists in this tree. `scripts/release-set.mjs:82–95` accepts only pending/done and refuses unresolved inherited gates. `scripts/release-record.mjs:59–69` independently requires the same final reference after package publication. Therefore changing one checklist row or only preflight would not implement the decision and could leave the post-publication record path failing. Current source correctly refuses the incomplete old chain; this is a known policy-transition blocker, not a newly found application/security flaw. The existing burn-in inputs authenticate a published RC plus D14. The lead has now explicitly clarified that the planned transition preserves beta → audited published RC → final and moves only the RC soak's timing after final; it does not require a replacement final-set burn-in authentication path.

   Resolve with one explicitly scoped, independently reviewed representation and implementation that preserves truthful deferred status, real published RC/P17/D14, the final diff binding, exact package/producer/digest authentication, immutable tags/OIDC, and the unchanged 3600 ACTIVE-second workloads for later verification. Reconcile authoritative release prose and retain the actual founder decision. Alternatively, complete the original chain. No fabricated audit/soak pass or generic bypass is acceptable. The implementation and its exact final delta will need review before release acceptance. The lead reports this implementation in progress and an RC-version restoration on a separate branch; neither is represented by the ee7 tree reviewed here.

4. **Final factual closure remains future work.** Close remaining final cleanup/measurement rows only against actual evidence. Trusted publication, all seven registry byte checks, the eventual deferred verification and final as-built reconciliation have not occurred. The current v3 file is explicitly a checkpoint record. Application migrations remain excluded and the final as-built/hard-halt boundary remains in force.

The separate operational L60 deferrals and FORMA-207 unknown historical ReadingMode cause remain as recorded, without turning them into new pre-release product defects. The original 2461.377-second beta.4 outer-target miss remains a miss, distinct from P17 and maintainer effort.

## Review hold

The source review for the stated ee7 tree is complete to the bounded scope above and in `INTERIM-SUBSTANTIVE-REVIEW.md`. Await the two current original campaign results and the separately reviewed policy implementation/final delta. Do not serialize this note as `accepted:true`, mark the whole-release audit gate done, or bind a later changed tree to it. No product files, application repositories, remote state, workflows, tags or publication were changed by this auditor.

## Findings

- **D14-001: resolved.** The separate P17 hard clock, outer-release target and maintainer-effort distinction remains intact.
- **D14-002: resolved by the actual completion implementation.** `scripts/release-soak-completion.mjs` now provides the supported later-verification CLI/helper missing at 43f3. No blocking source finding remains from this bounded review.

## Resolution verified

The consumer requires an exact clean `v3.0.0` checkout, matching local final and RC tags, a committed regular deferred reference and canonical independently reviewed final diff. It accepts only positive safe run/attempt identities and a concrete manifest hash. A fresh absolute output directory must be outside the checkout after resolving its parent symlinks; it refuses overwrite, relative paths and in-checkout output before API reads.

It authenticates actual final GitHub release metadata, final DS12 and deferred-reference asset sizes/digests/bytes. Final tag/commit/classification and exact deferred/zero-credit/no-pass disposition must match the committed reference. It rejects a simultaneous completed-burn-in claim. It then reuses the real RC authenticator for the same published archives/P17/D14 and compares all three authenticated digests to that reference. The final immutable DS12/reference are read, not rewritten.

The existing hosted-evidence downloader verifies the exact successful RC burn-in source/ref/workflow/event/attempt, required successful workload step, original artifact digest and nested manifest. The new consumer additionally requires valid UTC run creation and attempt-start times at or after the original final publication, with start at or after creation. Raw expected inputs, package identities, actual archived runtime bytes, RC Git harness inventory, all workload proofs, 3600 ACTIVE seconds, zero faults and complete owned cleanup are checked through the shared validator.

I independently compared the extracted `validateAuthenticatedBurnIn` body with its previous inline implementation: it is identical after whitespace and replacing the local result assignment with a return. The completed-soak route uses the same checks. The final reference remains zero/false; only the separate successful `verification.json` records actual later credit, rounds, cleanup and final/RC/run/artifact identities. Failures retain acquired evidence and an error receipt, never a successful receipt. The documented CLI and operational sequence match the implementation.

`docs/RELEASING.md` now consistently distinguishes the exact deferred soak from done gates and describes its authentic RC/P17/audit/final-diff prerequisites. It no longer implies all gates passed under this exception. No live release-contract gate or real reference was created by these source changes.

## Evidence and limitations

Read `work/FORMA-final-post-release-soak/COMPLETION-RESULT.txt`, the exact source/tests, and both original completion logs. The first dedicated run has eight passes/three failures caused by incomplete synthetic skew proof and a mismatched negative expectation; it remains retained. The final exact candidate's focused run passed 31/31 in 74.043135542 seconds, with no skipped or cancelled cases: eleven dedicated deferral/completion controls, seven existing final-diff controls and thirteen existing burn-in-report controls. Those tests use real Git/tar/ZIP/manifest operations with explicitly synthetic API/workload records and an injected RC network seam. They establish validator behavior, not actual founder approval, publication or 3600 seconds of executed stress. The earlier 325-helper receipt is not relabeled as a run of this completion source. No heavy tests or campaigns were rerun by the reviewer.

Positive and refusal controls exercise the supported CLI, exact final assets/reference, immutable original disposition, RC proof digests, failed/wrong producer and steps, pre-publication/malformed clocks, manifest disagreement, short or incomplete/faulted workloads, unfinished cleanup, raw semantic failures, dirty/wrong-tag checkout and unsafe output. Existing normal-path validation remained intact. Static diff checks pass. `COMPLETION-DELTA-RECHECK-62be639f.json` retains the comparison scope.

## R17 and qualification scope

No product/version/dependency/fixture/indexed/parity inputs, R17 command list, ordinary CI workflow, or existing timed tests changed between 43f3 and 62be. The new completion CLI is not invoked by R17. Added cases remain in the dedicated release-policy test file selected by the separate release-workflow job. The shared helper extraction leaves existing ordinary record/final branches semantically unchanged, although module bytes and theoretically import/dispatch overhead are not identical.

The earlier bounded applicability conclusion therefore still holds: a successful ee7 twenty-command result can support the unchanged R17 workload with explicit original measured-source identity and actual composed-source R17 CI; it is not an exact 62be elapsed-time measurement or proof of zero overhead. No duplicate twenty-run campaign is justified solely by this completion patch. The lead reports run `39285416133` now successful, but its raw artifact review was not yet supplied when this source disposition was written. I do not independently certify its numeric result here.

Whole-release acceptance remains pending review of the original current P17 and twenty-run artifacts, current composed CI, and truthful exact-source evidence applicability. Future RC publication, canonical final preparation/reference and its independent review, trusted final publication, and the real later soak/v3 completion remain required operational steps. No application migration, remote action, workflow dispatch or product edit was performed by this reviewer.

# Independent Actions archive media-negotiation review

**Approve the focused source fix `8bca031e71b98063a35140a7896a5357e768cd0e` for the required CI and RC.2 preparation.** Tree `2656433f5f512085864055be42ec6478a6470f39`; parent is immutable RC.1 commit `dac3b683639714aab7398107dc981e60e0111727`. Checkout is clean. No blocking defect was found in this two-file patch. This is focused source approval, not acceptance of an unprepared RC.2/final tree or certification of the in-progress live authentication.

**D14-003 — medium, resolved in this source patch; immutable RC.1 remains affected.** The real post-publication read of Actions artifact `12211117257` failed with HTTP415 when `releaseReader` requested the ZIP endpoint using `Accept: application/octet-stream`. The retained diagnostic identifies successful Release `39298323413`, an unexpired `release-p17` archive and the actual415 response. This is a release-evidence acquisition defect, not a P17/registry publication failure or a completed burn-in. Root's live comparison found the JSON API media type obtains the archive redirect. [Original diagnostic](/Users/victorvillacis/dev/Forma/work/FORMA-rc1-publication/INITIAL-DOWNLOAD-DIAGNOSTIC.json).

The production delta only detects the repository's Actions artifact `/zip` URL and uses `application/vnd.github+json` for its API negotiation. Response handling remains binary. Ordinary API JSON behavior and release assets' `application/octet-stream` behavior remain intact. The existing upstream archive URL validator requires the exact repository, positive artifact id and `/zip` suffix, so this narrow branch is exercised by authenticated Actions inventory rather than an arbitrary new endpoint.

Inspected the complete acquisition path: same API-origin restriction, authorization header, request timeout, response success refusal, declared/actual byte ceilings, evidence-room accounting, exclusive output creation, streaming hash, archive inventory size/digest comparison, bounded extraction and nested manifest verification. Exact source/tag/workflow/event/run-attempt/job/step checks and release/registry/D14 authentication remain unchanged. There is no retry, size/threshold relaxation, swallowed error, policy bypass, new trust source or altered workload.

The new regression calls the actual reader with a fetch seam that refuses the old header with415. It checks the Actions streamed download's exact bytes/hash and the ordinary release-asset binary result, while preserving the authorization value. This verifies media selection and unchanged byte handling; the fixture returns bytes directly and does not itself prove a live redirect. Actual GitHub authentication remains the separately running owner operation.

Read both retained original logs. Before: six passes and the new regression fails with `artifact download failed`. After: fourteen passes, zero failures/skips/cancellations, in 9947.680375 ms. The actual after-log scope is **seven input-reader controls plus seven existing final-binding/fixture controls**; it does not contain the eleven dedicated soak-deferral/completion tests. It must not be described as a complete rerun of those dedicated cases. The full required release-workflow CI selects this input test and the dedicated policy tests through its existing `scripts/release*.test.mjs` glob. No tests were rerun by this reviewer. [Before](/Users/victorvillacis/dev/Forma/work/FORMA-rc1-publication/ARTIFACT-MEDIA-BEFORE.log), [after](/Users/victorvillacis/dev/Forma/work/FORMA-rc1-publication/ARTIFACT-MEDIA-AFTER.log).

Audit impact is explicit: this release helper and test change are outside the old D14 evidence-only descendant allowlist. The existing RC.1 acceptance and published assets must remain immutable historical records; they do not automatically qualify the changed verifier or conceal this newly discovered operational defect. RC.1's hosted soak runner checks out its own immutable source and retains the bad header. Preparing a new RC.2 with the corrected helper, canonical RC.2 metadata and a new exact-source review/input binding is appropriate. Do not retag RC.1 or carry the changed helper only in final while claiming the old RC's hosted consumer is repaired.

The fix changes no product/compiler/runtime/native bytes, P17 collector, indexed threshold, benchmark command or R17 test inventory. The added input test runs in the separate release-workflow job, not the timed R17 list. This alone does not justify inventing a new twenty-command campaign; applicability to the later composed RC.2 still requires its actual delta/current-CI review. The reviewed 71e4035e final preparation was against RC.1 and likewise needs rebasing/rebinding to the eventual authentic RC.2 source and evidence.

Root must retain the actual corrected authentication result, prepare the full RC.2 source/evidence composition, obtain its required CI and review, and publish/qualify that immutable set before using it in the eventual final reference. Soak credit remains zero. No source edit, campaign, download, checkout mutation or remote action was performed by this reviewer.

The original whole-release v2/decision review, actual L65 initialization, product/security/ownership/compiler/native/browser source analysis, prior pipeline/deferral/completion reviews and their honest scope remain applicable to the unchanged implementation. ## Findings and resolutions

The only follow-up source change identifies RC.2 while retaining RC.3 publication-pending wording. Original D14-001 through D14-004 and their actual resolved evidence remain intact: distinct P17/outer-clock/human-effort claims, supported authentic later soak completion, repaired Actions media negotiation and the historical RC.2 README correction.
